notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Make every technical claim traceable before it becomes an asset.
intro: A proposed marketing-agent workbench for Traversal: connect buyer questions to current product evidence, scoped claims and a human review path.
queueIntro: All account and asset examples are synthetic. This portfolio does not investigate real incidents, connect to infrastructure or perform remediation.
workbenchIntro: Review evidence and audience fit before proposing content. Generated copy is a draft; local acceptance does not publish anything or grant an agent authority to do so.
firstBody: Combine approved product context, a technical buyer question and a source-version record so reviewers can verify claims before an asset enters a campaign.

fields.label: Technical buyer and intended question defined
Product claim has an approved source and version
Claim stays within the evidence scope
Example uses safe synthetic operating context
Asset and next action match the buyer stage

rules.title: Define the technical audience
rules.next: Separate an SRE practitioner’s investigation question from a platform leader’s evaluation criteria.

rules.title: Ground the technical claim
rules.next: Attach current product evidence. Do not turn a draft or old competitive note into a public capability claim.

rules.title: Narrow the claim to what is supported
rules.next: Avoid universal outage-prevention or remediation promises when the source supports a narrower scenario.

rules.title: Remove private operating details
rules.next: Use fictional system examples, not customer incident logs, credentials or internal infrastructure details.

rules.title: Route the asset for technical review
rules.next: A generated asset needs an accountable technical reviewer before publication.

rules.title: Match the next step to the reader
rules.next: Use an educational next step for a learning-stage reader and an evaluation path for an active buyer.

ready.title: Ready for technical content review
ready.next: The named reviewer can inspect the claim, source scope, audience and next action. Publishing remains a separate approved step.

experiments.name: Evidence-attached content proposals
experiments.hypothesis: Sources and scope reduce unsupported technical claims.
experiments.treatment: Claim, evidence version and explicit limitation
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Buyer-stage content paths
experiments.hypothesis: A useful next step connects education to qualified interest.
experiments.treatment: Educational or evaluation CTA matched to intent
experiments.guardrail: Low-quality form fills and misleading attribution
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Build the approved context library
roadmap.body: Work with marketing and technical stakeholders on product sources, competitive evidence and claim boundaries.

roadmap.title: Pilot a narrow marketing agent
roadmap.body: Generate one asset type with an evidence trail and human review. Measure corrections before expanding formats.

roadmap.title: Connect content to commercial learning
roadmap.body: Track account engagement through qualified conversations without treating impressions as pipeline. Refresh sources and evaluate cost.
roadmap.measure: Useful content, qualified outcomes and review effort

records.name: Alder Platform
records.context: A synthetic guide explains questions to ask when evaluating incident-investigation tooling.
records.question: Which evidence would help a platform leader evaluate the approach?

records.name: Cedar Reliability
records.context: A draft blends executive buying criteria with a troubleshooting tutorial.
records.question: Who is the intended reader and what do they need next?

records.name: Willow Systems
records.context: The asset cites an old product note with no approved version.
records.question: Which current source supports the claim?

records.name: Elm Cloud
records.context: A draft promises that all incidents will be prevented.
records.question: What narrower claim does the evidence support?

records.name: Birch Engineering
records.context: The example was copied from a private incident record.
records.question: Can a fictional scenario explain the same idea?

records.name: Juniper Infrastructure
records.context: A technically grounded asset lacks an assigned reviewer.
records.question: Who can approve the claim before publication?

metricsTitle: Separate asset quality, engagement and qualified demand.
metricsIntro: Synthetic marketing-agent scorecard for a fixed pilot window.
metricsNotes: These numbers are invented and do not represent Traversal performance or customer incident outcomes.
An asset acceptance rate is not permission for autonomous publication.
Track source version, reviewer effort and errors alongside cost per accepted proposal.
